documents.unit: Old Dominion University Board of Visitors (EVMS is now part of ODU)
documents.title: Policy 1220 Standards for the Safe Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: ODU Board of Visitors policy setting institution-wide AI standards for employees: ethics, innovation, privacy, equity, vendor review and research data. It says little about student coursework and sets no rules on student AI use.
documents.stance_why: The document sets standards for employees and "Encourage[s] innovation and experimentation in AI integration" while requiring safeguards for privacy and vendors; it neither bans nor delegates, and is permissive in spirit, so encourage.

units.why: The stated purpose frames the whole policy as building "a culture of integrity" with "responsible, ethical, and transparent use" of AI, an institution-wide principle rather than a rule, so P56.
units.anchor: establish a culture of integrity that ensures the responsible, ethical, and transparent use of artificial
units.resolution_why: Both coded P56/informs/neutral; actor differed (A all, B admin). The purpose clause states the aim of the whole University policy and the policy applies to all, so actor is all.

units.why: The definition section says what AI is ("the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines"), which sets what the policy covers, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: the simulation of human intelligence processes by machines

units.why: Scope sentence states who the policy binds ("all Old Dominion University employees"), which sets its reach and notably excludes students; P61 (scope) fits.
units.anchor: applies to all Old Dominion University employees

units.why: The scope also names research, education and administration as covered areas, extending the policy to "educational initiatives"; same scope type P61, kept separate from the who-clause.
units.anchor: This scope extends to AI applications in research endeavors, educational initiatives, administrative functions
units.resolution_why: Only A coded the second scope sentence (research, educational initiatives, administrative functions). It is a separate scope statement from the who-clause, so kept as P61.

units.why: The policy statement commits to AI standards that "support research, teaching, and administration"; a principle-level framework statement, hence P56.
units.anchor: committed to the effective implementation of comprehensive artificial intelligence policy standards
units.frag_end: protecting individual data, and mitigating risk.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the commitment sentence of the Policy Statement. It states the University is committed to standards that "support research, teaching, and administration", a principle-level statement, so kept as P56.

units.why: Standard 1 says the standards will "Prioritize ethical considerations and ethical use" in teaching, learning and research, an institution-level principle (P56) rather than a specific bias concern (P53).
units.anchor: Prioritize ethical considerations and ethical use in AI deployment, in teaching, learning, research, and administration
units.resolution_why: A coded P56, B coded P53. The item says to prioritize ethical considerations "promoting fairness, accountability, transparency and respect for human rights", an institution-wide principle rather than a naming of specific harms; P53 does not fit as well, so P56.

units.why: Standard 2 states the university will "Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration" in teaching and learning; this is a default pro-AI stance, P02.
units.anchor: Encourage innovation and experimentation in AI integration to enhance teaching, learning, and research outcomes

units.why: Standard 3 commits to "Safeguard the privacy and security of individuals' data" with data protection measures; privacy and protection fits P50.
units.anchor: Safeguard the privacy and security of individuals' data by implementing robust data protection measures

units.why: Standard 4 requires strategies to mitigate AI risks "including biases, discrimination, and data breaches", naming bias harms, so P53.
units.anchor: mitigate risks associated with AI technologies, including biases, discrimination, and data breaches

units.why: Standard 5 says to "Ensure equitable access to AI resources and opportunities for all students, faculty, and staff", an access/equity rule, P51.
units.anchor: Ensure equitable access to AI resources and opportunities for all students, faculty, and staff
units.resolution_why: The six standards share the lead-in "These standards will:" and every other item was coded should by both coders; B alone coded this one must and A alone coded stance encourage. The text has no "must" and the item states an equity principle, so should and neutral.

units.why: Standard 6 says to "Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences", a welcoming default use of AI for learning (P02); P44 does not fit because it is about students' professional skill.
units.anchor: Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences, cater to diverse learner needs, and improve student
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B coded admin. "Leverage AI technologies to personalize learning experiences" invites anyone using AI in education, as the sibling "Encourage innovation" item does, so actor all.

units.why: The procedure requires a "standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI technologies", a review of AI procurement, so P65.
units.anchor: shall establish a standardized and transparent approval process for the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of
units.resolution_why: A coded P65, B coded P50. The item sets an approval process for "the acquisition, development, and/or deployment of AI technologies" with Procurement and IT review; this is review of acquisitions (P65), not protection of personal data (P50). It gates deployment, so restrict.

units.why: AI outputs in educational settings "must be accompanied by clear and comprehensive disclaimers" about limitations and biases; this is closest to P31 (outputs can be wrong or biased) rather than P24, since it labels output limits, not student use.
units.anchor: must be accompanied by clear and comprehensive disclaimers that inform users about the limitations, assumptions,
units.resolution_why: Both coded P31; stance differed (A require, B neutral). The disclaimer rule labels AI output with its limitations and does not require or permit AI use, so neutral.

units.why: The same item says disclaimers must "clarify the roles and responsibilities of human users in interpreting and acting upon AI-generated information", placing responsibility on the human user, P29 fits.
units.anchor: clarify the roles and responsibilities of human users in interpreting and acting upon AI -generated
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this second clause of the same sentence. It makes a separate rule, that disclaimers "clarify the roles and responsibilities of human users", which fits P29 (human responsibility). Kept; stance neutral since it does not set a position on AI use.

units.why: Item 2b commits to "Promote transparency in AI usage" by sharing information on AI applications and decision-making, a general principle (P56).
units.anchor: Promote transparency in AI usage by providing stakeholders with access to information about AI applications

units.why: Item 3a requires assessing and mitigating third-party vendor risks, including "data sharing agreements, contractual obligations", which is vendor review (P65).
units.anchor: assess and mitigate risks associated with third -party AI vendors
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A should, B must). Procedure F3a is an unqualified imperative ("Implement measures to assess and mitigate risks") under Procedures, like F1 "shall establish", so must.

units.why: Item 3b says vendor contracts "should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards", a contract-level rule, P65.
units.anchor: Contracts with AI vendors should include provisions for data protection, privacy safeguards

units.why: Item 3c calls for "regular audits and assessments" of third-party AI performance and security, a recurring review of vendors (P65; P54 is about the policy itself).
units.anchor: Conduct regular audits and assessments in collaboration with ITS to monitor the performance and security
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A should, B must). "Conduct regular audits and assessments" is an unqualified imperative under Procedures, so must.

units.why: Item 4a requires "robust data privacy and security measures" for sensitive information processed by AI systems, P50.
units.anchor: Implement robust data privacy and security measures to safeguard sensitive information
units.resolution_why: Both coded P50/must; stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). The item tells the institution to implement privacy measures and does not restrict AI use itself, so neutral.

units.why: Item 4b requires AI systems to "comply with applicable laws" on student data such as FERPA and HIPAA, a data protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: AI systems comply with applicable laws and regulations governing the collection, storage, and use of
units.resolution_why: Both coded P50/must; stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). It requires AI systems to comply with FERPA, GDPR and HIPAA, a compliance duty and not a restriction on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Procedure 5a calls for stronger data privacy "when using AI technologies" in research and "informed consent"; research governance, P62.
units.anchor: Strengthen provisions related to data privacy and security when using AI technologies,
units.resolution_why: A anchored "obtaining informed consent..." and B anchored "Strengthen provisions related to data privacy and security when using AI", but both lie in the same sentence (item 5a) and rule, so merged into one P62 unit. A coded stance restrict, B neutral; the sentence strengthens provisions and does not limit AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Item 5b says protected data must "not [be] entered into any AI research tool without proper risk analysis", a data-protection prohibition (P50) in the research setting.
units.anchor: confidential, sensitive, and other protected data are not entered into any AI research tool without
units.resolution_why: A coded P50, B coded P62. The rule keeps "confidential, sensitive, and other protected data" out of AI tools without risk analysis; that is data protection (P50). The research-governance side is covered by the separate P62 units for items 5a and 5c.

units.why: Item 5c says AI use in research with humans or animals "should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application", AI-in-research governance, P62.
units.anchor: should be disclosed in the Institutional Review Board (IRB) application

units.why: Implementation 6a promises "training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators on AI ethics", which supports people in learning AI, P63.
units.anchor: Provide training and professional development opportunities for faculty, staff, and administrators on AI ethics
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A should, B must) and stance (A neutral, B encourage). Item 6 lists "strategies" supporting implementation, written as institutional aims without "must", so should; providing training does not take a position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Item 6b says to "Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions" to share AI practices; no type covers partnerships for knowledge exchange (P65 is about contracts and data sharing), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions to exchange knowledge
units.uncovered_note: Institutional partnerships with industry, government and other universities to exchange AI knowledge and best practices.

units.why: Procedure 6c sets "ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives" and soliciting stakeholder feedback; review and feedback, P54.
units.anchor: ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives
units.resolution_why: Only B coded "ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives" as its own unit (A coded only the following feedback sentence). It is a real review rule under strategy 6c, P54. B coded must; strategies are phrased as aims, so should, consistent with its sibling units.

units.why: Item 6c sets up "ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and review of AI initiatives" and asks stakeholders for feedback to revise policy, which is a revisit-regularly rule, P54.
units.anchor: Solicit feedback from stakeholders and incorporate lessons learned into future AI projects and policies
units.resolution_why: Only A coded the feedback sentence ("Solicit feedback from stakeholders and incorporate lessons learned into future AI projects and policies"). It is a real separate sentence and a revisit-the-policy rule, so kept as P54.

units.why: Item 7 engages students and staff in "discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy, and societal implications"; it is community outreach with no matching type (P54 is policy revision), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Engage students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions and forums on AI ethics,
units.uncovered_note: Hold community discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy and societal implications.

units.why: Item 8 says the specific compliance standards "are published on the Information Technology Services Computing Policies and Standards website", pointing to the framework's detail, P56.
units.anchor: The specific standards to be utilized for compliance with this policy are published on the

units.why: Section G says the Division "shall conduct annual reviews of this policy", a review cycle, P54.
units.anchor: The Division shall conduct annual reviews of this policy

documents.unit: Old Dominion University AI Implementation Workgroup
documents.title: Guidelines for Teaching and Learning with AI
documents.summary: ODU guidelines encouraging faculty to explore AI and to put a clear AI statement in each syllabus. They give three sample course policies (permissive, hybrid, restrictive) and leave the choice to each instructor.
documents.stance_why: "Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses" and the document offers "Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use", so the decision is handed to instructors and tiers are listed.

units.why: The guidelines open by saying they give "clear and practical guidance" for AI in teaching and learning with an "innovative, ethical, and supportive environment"; a framework preamble, P56.
units.anchor: designed to foster an innovative, ethical, and supportive
units.frag_end: environment for AI use in education.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the opening statement that the guidelines are "designed to foster an innovative, ethical, and supportive environment for AI use in education". It is a framework preamble (P56), kept. B coded actor admin, but the guidelines address faculty, students and staff, so all.

units.why: Principle 1 says "Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools", a welcoming default for instructors, so P02.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to explore and integrate AI tools

units.why: Principle 2 requires AI use to "respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)", a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations (FERPA, HIPAA, etc.)
units.resolution_why: Both coded P50/should; stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). The sentence says AI use should "respect data privacy, and comply with relevant regulations", a compliance principle that does not limit AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "Transparency in AI applications is essential" is a principle stated without saying who discloses what; P56 as general framework.
units.anchor: Transparency in AI applications is essential

units.why: Principle 3 gives "Faculty ... the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in their courses", handing the decision to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Faculty have the autonomy to decide the extent to which they incorporate AI tools in

units.why: Faculty who do not use AI "will not be required to follow these guidelines": it leaves the extent of AI use to each instructor, which is the instructor-sets-the-rule type P04 (it also limits the scope of the guidelines, but its point is faculty choice), a fact so informs.
units.anchor: Those who choose not to use AI will not be required
units.resolution_why: A coded P61 (scope) and actor instructor/general, B coded P04/before-course. The sentence is the second half of the "Flexibility and Autonomy" principle, whose point is faculty choice, so P04 and before-course.

units.why: "Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided" is a commitment by the University to support faculty and students in learning AI, so P63. It states a fact ("will continue to be provided"), not an obligation, so informs, and it takes no position on AI use.
units.anchor: Comprehensive training programs and resources will continue to be provided
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general and modality informs, B coded before-course and must. "will continue to be provided" is a statement of fact, so informs; training supports setting up courses, so before-course; P63 agreed.

units.why: DTT will provide AI training and "Faculty are encouraged to attend these sessions", a faculty-support recommendation, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to attend these sessions

units.why: Principle 5 says "Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives", a revisit-and-improve commitment, P54.
units.anchor: Feedback on AI tools, trainings, and resources will be used to continuously improve AI initiatives

units.why: Faculty "should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools", advice that instructors learn AI before use, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty should familiarize themselves with the capabilities and limitations of AI tools

units.why: "AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment" says AI must not replace human thinking, which matches P32 (stay the primary thinker); it is not about instructors' teaching work (P59). It is addressed to everyone using AI, so all.
units.anchor: AI tools should be used to augment, not replace, human interaction and judgment.
units.resolution_why: A coded P59/instructor, B coded P32/all. The sentence is a general principle that AI augments rather than replaces human judgment, not a rule about what instructors use AI for in teaching tasks, so P32 and all. Stance neutral since it does not restrict specific uses.

units.why: "Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi" is a syllabus statement requirement, P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should include a clear AI policy in their course syllabi

units.why: "Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided" gives three named levels of AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: Sample policy statements for permissive, hybrid, and restrictive use are provided below

units.why: "Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate" asks instructors to restructure assignments around AI, P35.
units.anchor: Redesign assignments to leverage AI tools where appropriate

units.why: "design assignments to promote original student work" given the potential for misuse is also assignment redesign around AI, P35.
units.anchor: design assignments to promote original student work
units.resolution_why: Both coded P35/should; stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). Designing assignments "to promote original student work" is a design duty and does not ban AI, so neutral.

units.why: "Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse" tells instructors to state expectations to students, P09 (communicating) rather than P37 since no penalties are given.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate expectations regarding the use of AI tools and the consequences of misuse

units.why: "Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards" routes AI misconduct into the existing integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: Academic integrity misconduct will follow existing honor code and student conduct standards

units.why: "Faculty will be provided with relevant tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct related to AI" is a University commitment to equip faculty with detection tools, so P40, an admin duty stated as fact (informs).
units.anchor: tools and trainings to detect and address potential academic misconduct related to AI
units.resolution_why: A coded actor instructor, B coded admin. Faculty are the recipients; the one who acts (provides tools and trainings) is the University, so admin.

units.why: "Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws" covers IP and legal compliance, P52.
units.anchor: Ensure AI use complies with copyright, intellectual property, and privacy laws
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality (A should, B must) and stance (A restrict, B neutral). The Guidelines use "should" and no "must"; the line is a legal-compliance principle, not a limit on AI use, so should and neutral.

units.why: "Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations when using AI tools in teaching and learning" is a data protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Protect sensitive data and comply with FERPA and HIPAA regulations when using AI tools in
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A during-work, B general), modality (A should, B must) and stance (A restrict, B neutral). The sentence applies "when using AI tools in teaching and learning", so during-work; the document uses should; it is a compliance duty, so neutral.

units.why: "Use AI tools in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility" is an equity requirement, P51.
units.anchor: Use AI tools in a manner that supports diversity, inclusion, and accessibility

units.why: The item tells instructors to "Educate students and recommend student to attend trainings" on the ethical use of AI and "potential biases and limitations of AI-generated content", so P53 (bias and limits), with instructor as actor; it does not take a position on AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: Educate students and recommend student to attend trainings
units.policy: Faculty educate students and recommend that students attend trainings on the ethical use of AI and the potential biases and limitations of AI-generated content.
units.resolution_why: A anchored the educating clause and B the bias clause of the same bullet, one rule. A coded stance encourage, B neutral; educating about bias is not a position on AI use, so neutral. The policy is normalized to include both parts.

units.why: "DTT will continue to update and add to the existing AI website" to include trainings and resources is a University commitment to support faculty (P63), stated as fact, so informs, and neutral toward AI use.
units.anchor: will continue to update and add to the existing AI website
units.resolution_why: A coded over-time/informs, B coded before-course/must. "will continue to update" is a statement of fact, so informs. The update is of support resources, not a policy review, so before-course like the other P63 units.

units.why: "Faculty can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions" and share their experience, a faculty community and support item, P63.
units.anchor: Faculty can coordinate with DTT to recommend or develop new training sessions

units.why: The permissive sample says the course "encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT for all assignments and assessments", open encouragement, P02.
units.anchor: encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT for
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A during-work, B course-start). The sample says the course "encourages students to explore the use of Generative AI" for assignments, a rule about doing the work, so during-work.

units.why: "Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited" requires disclosure of AI use in the submission, P24.
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited
units.resolution_why: Both coded P24/must; stance differed (A require, B permit). Acknowledgment is a condition on permitted use, which the codebook scores as permit. B also coded the identical sentence in the Hybrid sample; repeats are skipped under the codebook.

units.why: "It is each student's responsibility to assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output" requires verifying AI output, P31.
units.anchor: assess the validity and applicability of any GenAI output
units.resolution_why: Both coded P31/must; stance differed (A require, B permit). Verifying output is a condition on permitted use, so permit. B also coded the repeat in the Hybrid sample; skipped.

units.why: "you bear the final responsibility" makes the student answerable for what is submitted, P29.
units.anchor: you bear the final responsibility
units.resolution_why: Both coded P29/must; stance differed (A require, B neutral). "you bear the final responsibility" sets accountability and no position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: "Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct" classifies breaches as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: Violations of this policy will be considered academic misconduct

units.why: The hybrid sample says certain assignments "will permit or even encourage" GenAI while others do not, so permission is set assignment by assignment, P04.
units.anchor: Certain assignments in this course will permit or even encourage the use of Generative AI
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase (A during-work, B course-start). Assignments that "permit or even encourage" AI decide what is allowed while doing the work, so during-work.

units.why: "The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated" states the fallback when an assignment is silent, P06.
units.anchor: The default is that such use is disallowed unless otherwise stated

units.why: The restrictive sample says "all the work students submit for this course will be their own", ownership of submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: all the work students submit for this course will be their own
units.resolution_why: Both coded P29/must; stance differed (A require, B restrict). In the Restrictive sample "all the work students submit ... will be their own" bounds AI use, so restrict.

units.why: Restrictive sample: collaborative assignments must "list all team members who participated"; an authorship rule, P29 (work is own) fits better than P24, which is about AI disclosure.
units.anchor: we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded the sentence that collaborative assignments should "list all team members who participated". It is a real rule in the Restrictive sample about authorship of submitted work, P29, kept.

units.why: "We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI (GenAI) tools at all stages of the work process" is a blanket ban, P01.
units.anchor: We specifically forbid the use of ChatGPT or any other Generative AI (GenAI) tools at

documents.unit: Macon & Joan Brock Virginia Health Sciences at ODU
documents.title: Brock Virginia Health Sciences AI Guidelines
documents.summary: Thin capture of the health sciences school page: an intro supporting responsible AI integration, a note that it works within ODU Policy 1220, and a welcome naming covered roles. The substantive Core Principles were not in the saved text.
documents.stance_why: The captured text says only that VHS "supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools" and defers to ODU Policy 1220; it hands no decision to instructors and bans nothing, so permit. A coded permit and B delegates; B offered no delegation language in the saved text. The page is thin because the Core Principles were not captured.

units.why: The page opens by saying VHS at ODU "supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools" in clinical care, education and research, a general framework statement, P56. Only this intro was captured; the Core Principles are not in the saved text.
units.anchor: VHS at ODU supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A all, B admin) and stance (A permit, B encourage). "supports thoughtful, responsible integration of these tools" is a school-wide principle for everyone, so all; "supports ... responsible integration" welcomes AI with a condition, so permit.

units.why: "These guidelines operate within the ODU institutional framework" and point to Policy 1220 as authoritative, a scope and precedence statement, P56.
units.anchor: These guidelines operate within the ODU institutional framework
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on actor (A all, B admin). The note says the guidelines "operate within the ODU institutional framework", which defines their scope for all readers, so all.

units.why: The welcome sentence names the roles the guidance serves and says "practical guidance for each of these roles is here", which defines who the guidelines cover, so P61 scope, informs.
units.anchor: practical guidance for each of these roles is here
units.frag_start: Whether you are a clinician weighing
units.frag_end: for each of these roles is here.
units.policy: The guidelines give practical guidance for clinicians, biomedical researchers, clinical or teaching faculty preparing medical and health professions students for AI in healthcare, medical students, medical school staff, and authors addressing AI in scholarly and medical writing.
units.resolution_why: A anchored the medical-student clause (P61) and B the faculty clause (P44); both lie in one sentence listing the roles the guidance serves. That is one scope statement, not a rule that courses teach AI as a professional skill, so P61, with an anchor and policy covering the whole role list.

notes: EVMS now part of ODU. The VHS page text is thin (core principles not captured), so its coding is limited. v2-evms-specific.txt was not collected and not coded. No student-facing rule appears in BOV 1220; student-facing rules come from the ODU teaching guidelines samples. Reconciled from coders A and B. Third document (VHS at ODU) is thin: its Core Principles were collapsed content not captured in the saved text. The BOV 1220 scope covers employees only; student-facing rules come from the ODU teaching guidelines samples.
